headline: Funding flows. Risks rise. Satellites launch.
deck: A mix of funding successes and risk warnings dominate this week's space news.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, emphasizing its role in co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The round reflects growing demand from the Department of Defense for advanced surveillance capabilities. With a valuation of $1.6 billion, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the defense sector.
stories.soWhat: The cash influx indicates that DoD pull-through is not just a buzzword; it's becoming a reality for companies that can deliver.

stories.head: Pegasus launches Swift mission, but for how long?
stories.body: Pegasus successfully launched the Swift reboost mission, likely marking the end of the line for a rocket that has seen better days. The vehicle, once a staple of the small launch market, now faces increasing competition from more modern alternatives. With Pegasus's future in question, the industry is left wondering how long it can hold onto its legacy.
stories.soWhat: If Pegasus can't adapt, it might just become a footnote in the history of small launch vehicles.

stories.head: GAO flags Space Force's satellite cost concerns
stories.body: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) raised alarms about rising satellite costs and launch risks within the Space Force portfolio. This comes amid a $1.4 billion increase in the FY27 budget for space resilience, suggesting that lawmakers are finally taking note of the complexities involved. Managing these costs may soon require a degree in budgetary gymnastics.
stories.soWhat: If the GAO is worried, it might be time for the Space Force to start practicing its budgetary somersaults.

watchlist.title: Watch for True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With fresh funding, True Anomaly could expand its offerings or pursue strategic partnerships in the defense sector.

watchlist.title: Isar Aerospace's upcoming satellite launch
watchlist.body: The launch of the German-built Planet imaging satellite will test Isar’s capabilities and market positioning in a competitive landscape.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser timeline
watchlist.body: After clearing a critical design review, the focus now shifts to whether Sierra can launch before the next ice age.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension could signal further government reliance on established players in the defense tech space.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
